subject: Release plan: SDK patch releases + docs deploy (examples refresh)
body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 2, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Release plan: SDK patch releases + docs deploy (examples refresh)

Monica / Elliot,

Pulling together the release plan for the examples refresh (streaming + tools + structured output) across the SDK patch releases + docs deploy.

Proposed versions (patch-only, no breaking changes):
- Python SDK: 1.14.2
- TypeScript SDK: 0.9.5
- Go SDK: 0.6.3
- Docs site deploy: immediately after SDKs are live (same day), with changelog entry

High-level sequencing (to minimize “docs ahead of code” drift):
1) Merge SDK PRs + publish packages
2) Validate snippets (CI + quick smoke against staging)
3) Deploy docs + announce

Can you both confirm these versions are OK / consistent with what the SDK owners expect? If anyone already cut a release branch w/ different versions, I’ll adjust.

Attaching a v3 checklist + draft changelog text for review.

- Connor

Attachment: release-checklist_examples-refresh_v3.md
Attachment: draft-changelog_sdk-patches_and_docs-deploy.txt


---

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 2, 2026 at 9:31 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release plan: SDK patch releases + docs deploy (examples refresh)

Connor,

Versions look fine.

Couple constraints from my side:
- We should not ship docs until Python + TS packages are actually on npm/pypi (we’ve been burned by propagation delays).
- Make sure the changelog explicitly calls out the new streaming event iteration pattern + tool arg delta accumulation guidance (those are where support tickets cluster).

Elliot — can you confirm docs can land behind a quick rollback (revert deploy) if we see errors in the wild?

Monica


---

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 2, 2026 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release plan: SDK patch releases + docs deploy (examples refresh)

Yes — docs rollback is straightforward.

Plan:
- We deploy docs via the standard pipeline; rollback is “redeploy previous successful build” (we keep the last 20 builds).
- If we need to revert content specifically, we can also revert the docs PR(s) and redeploy.

One ask: please include in the release checklist a final “copy/paste run” on the public docs for Python/TS/Go once it’s deployed (we’ve had formatting regressions from the renderer).

Elliot


---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 2, 2026 at 10:27 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release plan: SDK patch releases + docs deploy (examples refresh)

Got it.

I’ll update the checklist to include:
- Wait for package propagation (PyPI + npm) before docs deploy
- Post-deploy copy/paste run on docs pages for all 3 languages

Draft changelog text (please edit):

SDKs (Python 1.14.2 / TS 0.9.5 / Go 0.6.3)
- Streaming examples updated to the canonical event model (token deltas + final response capture)
- Tool calling examples now show safe accumulation of tool_call argument deltas (handles partial JSON)
- Structured output examples include schema validation + retry strategy on parse/validation failures
- Troubleshooting guidance added for stream disconnects, timeouts, and proxy buffering

Docs
- Consolidated Streaming / Tools / Structured Output section with consistent terminology (“tool calling”)
- Replaced legacy snippets with runnable canonical examples (Python/TS/Go)

Rollback plan (proposed):
- Docs: redeploy previous successful build; optionally revert docs PRs (901/902/903/904)
- SDKs:
  - If we catch an issue pre-announce: yank / deprecate the patch release and republish a fixed patch (1.14.3 / 0.9.6 / 0.6.4)
  - If post-announce: publish fixed patch ASAP; add prominent note to docs changelog with workaround

Monica — any preference on the “yank vs ship forward” posture for PyPI/npm? (Go is modules so it’s effectively “ship forward” only.)

- Connor


---

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 2, 2026 at 11:05 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release plan: SDK patch releases + docs deploy (examples refresh)

Prefer “ship forward” unless it’s actively dangerous.

Rationale:
- Yank/deprecate tends to create more confusion than it resolves, and customers pin versions.
- If we ship forward quickly and docs clearly points to the latest patch, it’s less operational overhead.

Exception: if a release causes credential leakage patterns or encourages unsafe tool execution. (I don’t think we’re anywhere near that, but we should treat it as a hard stop.)

Monica


---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 8:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release plan: SDK patch releases + docs deploy (examples refresh)

Elliot — confirming target deploy window.

If SDKs publish by ~12pm PT, can docs deploy at ~1:30pm PT?

Also, can you add a short docsite banner note (not a marketing banner; just a callout on the pages) for 1 week pointing people to the new canonical examples + troubleshooting section? We can remove after support volume stabilizes.

- Connor


---

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 11:46 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release plan: SDK patch releases + docs deploy (examples refresh)

1:30pm PT works.

Re: callout — yes, we can add a lightweight note on the Streaming + Tools + Structured Output landing page (not global). Send me the final wording you want.

Suggested copy (edit as needed):
“Examples updated Feb 2026: canonical streaming event handling, tool argument delta aggregation, and structured output validation patterns. If you’re troubleshooting stream disconnects or partial tool args, see Troubleshooting.”

Once SDK releases are confirmed live, I’ll queue the deploy and we’ll do the post-deploy copy/paste checks you listed.

Elliot
